openingMessage: I don't look at myself as a basketball coach. I look at myself as a leader who happens to coach basketball.
openingWhy: You're not an H2S tech who happens to be standing on a location — you're the safety leader that roustabout crew is watching. The newest worm out there is learning this trade off your habits, not your words. You're teaching either way. Teach on purpose.
leadershipThought: Own your response. Own your equipment. Own your preparation. Own your outcome. Stay disciplined. Stay prepared. Protect each other.

exxonMoments:
Energy Isolation — 1099 Edward Carrillo [1099 Edward Carrillo] (Energy Isolation)
Crew followed SOP's. Verified LOTO, and continued good communications through task

Positive Observation — LOTO Disconnect Completed Efficiently (Energy Isolation)
LOTO, atmospheric testing, and hold points together form a complete energy control system — don't shortcut any one of them, even on a quick job.

Positive Observation — Well Disconnect Completed with No Issues (Energy Isolation)
LOTO and atmospheric monitoring together protect against both stored energy releases and unexpected gas exposure during disconnect operations.

Well Kill and Polished Rod Lift — Pressure Control Throughout (Energy Isolation)
Confirm the well is killed and on vacuum before breaking any connections — pressure verification at that step is not a formality.

Positive Observation — Full LOTO and Atmospheric Controls (Energy Isolation)
Verifying field conditions independently of paperwork is the discipline that keeps controls from becoming checkbox habits.

specialFocus.title: Happy Thanksgiving, Canon Family
specialFocus.why:
🦃 Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at Canon Safety.

“Happy Thanksgiving, Canon family. A lot of us get to sit down today with the people we do all of this for. That's the whole reason behind every bump test, every walk-around and every stop. And to everyone who can't be home today, on location, on nights, or a long way from your people: much love and good energy to you. We're thinking about you, and your plate is waiting.”
— Mike Lyons
🍂 THANKFUL FOR
  • The crews who stopped jobs this week and wrote it down, so the next crew knew.
  • Partners who watched each other's backs, every single shift.
  • Our families, who send us out before daylight and wait up for us to get home.
  • Dispatch, the office, the shops and training, who keep every truck rolling.
❤️ WORKING TODAY? Much love to you
  • Thank you. Somebody has to keep the field safe today, and it's you.
  • The holiday doesn't change the hazard. Same walk-around, same bump test, same stop work.
  • Call home on your break. Then get home safe to celebrate a day late. It still counts.
standard: Belt on, phone down, lights on. Holiday roads are full of tired, distracted drivers. Give them room.
Tired is impaired. Long drive to family? Swap drivers, or pull over and walk it off.
Frying a turkey? Outside, away from the house, fully thawed, and never left alone.
Check on somebody who can't be home. A two-minute call means more than you think.
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: Hug your people. Check on the ones who can't be with theirs. Thankful for every one of you. Happy Thanksgiving. We all go home.
